Twenty Fifth Indian Antarctic Expedition 2006-2007
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 23, pp 213-222
Ecological Study of Southern Pole Bird Skua and 
Penguins During Indian Antarctic Scientific 
Expedition to Antarctica
Ashok Surwade
MES Abasaheb Garware College, Pune 
ABSTRACT
During summer season of Antarctic weather, southern pole Skua was 
monitored, for ecological aspects. Likenesting, chick feeding, food habits, 
behavior against harsh environment habits, and habitat were considered. Fecal 
matters of some species were collected during the observation period on 
Schirmacher oasis. Later on, it was analyzed microscopically for protozoan 
parasites. Habits of Skua were observed for parasite force behavior. Certain 
adlib observations are added.
INTRODUCTION
Studies on ecology of parasites are relatively not much focused. 
Parasites are seen to influence several aspects of host ecology. Parasites 
can potentially affect population growth of species, host competition and 
coexistence, predator prey relationship, evolution of sex and secondary 
sexual characters, inbreeding in host species, gregariousness and sociality 
etc. The study of parasites and parasitic diseases is important for 
management and conservation of wild life. A number of studies are 
restricted to the listing of parasites detected in faecal samples, while 
others remaui unpublished or inaccessible. Quantitive studies addressing 
ecology and relevant management questions are few (Watve and Sukumar 
1995, 97).
Avian life on Antarctica shows its peak during summer season i.e. 
November to March. Few species are dominant on continent. Among 
them are penguin, skua, and petrels. On Schirmacher oasis skua, penguin 
and petrels were observed during same period in XXV ISEA.
Antarctica is well known for her extreme conditions. It is a coldest, 
driest, windiest continent. Many factors make Antarctic ecosystem ideal

214 Ashok Surwade
for biological research. Their simplicity, for instance. Conditions are so 
harsh that few life forms survive above the ice. A simple, land-based 
ecosystem is easier to study. There are fewer variables to consider, so 
conclusions are easier to draw. Under the ice, though, ocean life is rich, 
complex, and abundant. The Southern Ocean with its pack ice zone is a 
most unusual and highly specialized habitat, with ecosystems of great 
intrinsic scientific interest and resources of commercial value, such as 
krill, squid and fish. The unusual environmental conditions found on 
Antarctica, such as extreme cold and extreme seasonal and daily light 
cycles, offer unique opportunities for the study.
DISCUSSION
Skua is an extraordinarily interesting group for scientists, particularly 
those interested studying in behaviour and evolution. Currently of special 
interest to scientists is their origin and relationship to the gulls. In the 
South Polar Skua, uniquely within the family, and almost without 
precedent within sea birds, lethal sibling aggression is common and 
results in brood reduction from two hatchlings to a single chick. In this 
siblicide the first hatched chick attacks the second one within a day or 
two of its hatching and either chases it from the nest area (the most 
common result) Parents may or may not intervene. Its common occurrence 
among Antarctic Skua populations suggests a similar selective factor is 
operating, with attacks triggered by hunger or malnutrition. (Cohen et al.,
